definitions.explanation: the temperature at which a liquid turns into a solid

examples.japanese: {水|みず}の{凝固点|ぎょうこてん}は{零度|れいど}だ。
examples.english: The freezing point of water is zero degrees.

examples.japanese: {塩|しお}を{加|くわ}えると{凝固点|ぎょうこてん}が{下|さ}がる。
examples.english: Adding salt lowers the freezing point.

examples.japanese: {凝固点|ぎょうこてん}{降下|こうか}の{原理|げんり}を{利用|りよう}して、{冬|ふゆ}の{道路|どうろ}に{融雪剤|ゆうせつざい}を{撒|ま}く。
examples.english: Using the principle of freezing-point depression, de-icing agents are spread on winter roads.

notes:
Composed of {凝固|ぎょうこ} (solidification; coagulation) + {点|てん} (point). A scientific term commonly encountered in school chemistry and physics. The concept of {凝固点|ぎょうこてん}{降下|こうか} (freezing-point depression) is a standard topic in Japanese science education.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {凝固点|ぎょうこてん}{降下|こうか}: freezing-point depression
- {凝固点|ぎょうこてん}が{下|さ}がる: the freezing point drops
- {凝固点|ぎょうこてん}に{達|たっ}する: to reach the freezing point
- {凝固点|ぎょうこてん}を{測定|そくてい}する: to measure the freezing point

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {融点|ゆうてん}: melting point — the temperature at which a solid becomes liquid (same temperature as the freezing point, viewed from the other direction)
- {沸点|ふってん}: boiling point — the temperature at which a liquid becomes gas
- {氷点|ひょうてん}: freezing point (of water specifically) — more colloquial than {凝固点|ぎょうこてん}
